name: Herpes zoster (shingles) confirmation
description: This is not a risk score. We're checking whether your symptoms match the typical pattern of shingles. If they do, you need antiviral treatment as soon as possible.
time_criticality: 72 hours — antivirals are most effective if started within 3 days of rash onset

citations.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Shingles (Herpes Zoster): clinical overview for health care providers.
Cohen JI. Clinical practice: Herpes zoster. N Engl J Med. 2013;369(3):255-263.

validated_population: Not a validated score. The pattern (painful one-sided rash in a band) follows CDC clinical guidance on typical herpes zoster.
self_report_note: Early shingles can be hard to recognize, and rashes from other causes can look similar. A clinician confirms the diagnosis by examining the rash.
license_note: Pattern logic and question wording are original to OLA BOT, based on the public guidance cited. Not a validated scoring instrument.

0_to_24h.text: Rash started less than 24 hours ago. About 2 days remain in the 72-hour window.

1_to_3d.text: Rash started 1–3 days ago. The 72-hour window is closing and may end today. Start treatment today.

4_to_7d.text: The 72-hour window has passed. Antivirals may still be offered, for example if new blisters are still forming. Pain control is now the priority.

over_7d.text: Rash started more than a week ago. Treatment focuses on pain control and preventing long-term nerve pain (postherpetic neuralgia).

timeline.label: Day 4+: less effective; focus on pain control

items.question: Do you have a painful rash or blistering on your skin?
items.help: Fluid-filled bumps or open sores, usually with burning or stabbing pain.

items.question: Does the rash follow a band or stripe on one side of your body (not crossing the middle)?
items.help: One arm? One side of your chest or back? One side of your face? Not both sides, and not all over.

items.question: Did you have burning, tingling, or severe pain in that area before the rash appeared?
items.help: Typically 1–2 days before the blisters appear.
items.trace_label: Pain or tingling before the rash (not required)

items.question: When did the rash first appear?
items.help: Antiviral medicine works best if started within 72 hours of the rash appearing.

items.question: Is the rash near your eye, on your forehead, or on the tip of your nose?
items.help: Shingles near the eye can damage vision and needs emergency care.
items.trace_label: Rash near eye, forehead, or tip of nose

items.question: Do you have any of these? (Select all that apply)
items.help: Leave all unchecked if none apply.

options.label: Signs of skin infection (pus, severe warmth, spreading redness)

scoring.pattern_text: Consistent with shingles if BOTH: a painful rash or blisters AND a one-sided band (dermatomal) distribution. Pain before the rash supports the pattern but is not required.
scoring.threshold_text: Pattern check, not a score. Routing: eye involvement, eye pain, or confusion/severe headache → emergency department; spreading rash, high fever, or infection → urgent care today; consistent pattern → antiviral treatment urgency set by days since rash onset.

levels.label: Pattern CONSISTENT with herpes zoster (shingles)
levels.interpretation: Your symptoms match the typical pattern of herpes zoster (shingles).

levels.label: Pattern NOT CONSISTENT with typical shingles
levels.interpretation: Your symptoms do not match the typical pattern of shingles. This does not rule it out, but the pattern is atypical.

steps.label: Rash near the eye, forehead, or tip of the nose
Rash spreading beyond one band, high fever, or signs of skin infection
Pattern consistent and rash started within 3 days (72-hour window open)
Pattern consistent and rash started 4–7 days ago
Pattern consistent and rash started more than 1 week ago

ed_eye.label: Emergency: shingles may involve the eye
ed_eye.interpretation: Shingles on the forehead, near the eye, or on the tip of the nose, or with eye pain or vision changes, can damage the eye and cause vision loss.
ed_eye.recommendation: Go to the emergency room now. Herpes zoster affecting the eye needs urgent evaluation, usually including an eye doctor.

care.where_detail: Hospital emergency department. An ophthalmologist (eye doctor) may need to examine the eye.

ed_neuro.label: Emergency: possible nerve or brain complication
ed_neuro.interpretation: Confusion or a severe headache with a shingles-like rash can mean the infection is affecting the brain or its lining.
ed_neuro.recommendation: Go to the emergency room now.

care.where_detail: Hospital emergency department. Call 911 if the person is very drowsy or confused.
ed_redirect: Very drowsy, hard to wake, or seizure: call 911

urgent_complication.label: Needs same-day care: possible complication
urgent_complication.interpretation: A rash spreading beyond one band, high fever, or signs of skin infection can mean a more serious or widespread infection. This is more common in people with weak immune systems.
urgent_complication.recommendation: See a clinician today, in person.

care.where_detail: Urgent care clinic, or emergency department if you feel very unwell or have a weak immune system (for example, cancer treatment or transplant medicines).
ed_redirect: Rash near the eye, eye pain, or vision changes
Confusion, severe headache, or stiff neck
Weakness of the face or limbs

antiviral_today.label: Shingles pattern: start antivirals today
antiviral_today.interpretation: Your symptoms match the typical pattern of shingles, and you are within or at the edge of the 72-hour antiviral window.
antiviral_today.recommendation: See a clinician today or tomorrow to start antiviral medication. The 72-hour window for maximum effectiveness is closing.

care.where_detail: Urgent care, a same-day primary care visit, or a telehealth urgent care visit (shingles can often be diagnosed by video).
ed_redirect: Rash near the eye, eye pain, or vision changes
Confusion, severe headache, or stiff neck
Weakness of the face or limbs
self_care: Keep the rash clean and covered.
Avoid contact with pregnant people, newborns, and people with weak immune systems until the blisters crust over; the virus can spread to them as chickenpox.
Acetaminophen or ibuprofen as labeled for pain.

primary_week.label: Shingles pattern: see primary care this week
primary_week.interpretation: Your symptoms match the typical pattern of shingles. The 72-hour window has passed, but treatment can still help.
primary_week.recommendation: See your primary care clinician this week. Pain management is now the priority.

care.where_detail: Primary care clinic or telehealth visit.
ed_redirect: Rash near the eye, eye pain, or vision changes
Confusion, severe headache, or stiff neck
Weakness of the face or limbs
self_care: Keep the rash clean and covered until it crusts over.
Avoid contact with pregnant people, newborns, and people with weak immune systems until the blisters crust over.

primary_routine.label: Shingles pattern: focus on pain and recovery
primary_routine.interpretation: Your symptoms match the typical pattern of shingles. The rash began more than a week ago.
primary_routine.recommendation: See your primary care clinician within the next 1 to 2 weeks. Focus is on managing pain and preventing long-term nerve pain (postherpetic neuralgia).

ed_redirect: Rash near the eye, eye pain, or vision changes
Confusion, severe headache, or stiff neck
Weakness of the face or limbs
self_care: Ask about the shingles vaccine once you recover; it lowers the chance of shingles returning.

evaluate.label: Rash pattern is not typical of shingles
evaluate.interpretation: Your symptoms do not match the typical pattern of shingles. This does not rule it out, but the pattern is atypical.
evaluate.recommendation: See a clinician to identify what is causing your rash.

care.where_detail: Primary care or urgent care clinic.
ed_redirect: Rash near the eye, eye pain, or vision changes
Confusion, severe headache, or stiff neck
Weakness of the face or limbs
Rash with fever that spreads quickly, or skin that turns purple or blisters widely
